newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Guide to the Bulgarian presidential elections.
newsitem.headline: Guide to the Bulgarian presidential elections.

text.p: Bulgaria votes on Sunday in a second round run-off of presidential elections, its second since the end of communist rule in 1989. Here are some key facts and figures on the election:
Polling stations will open from 6 a.m. (0400 GMT) to 7 p.m. (1700 GMT). Votes will be counted in polling stations then collated by regional offices of the Central Electoral Committee.

First projections from independent polling institutions are expected around 1800 GMT. Preliminary official results are expected early on Monday and full official results must be announced within 48 hours.

Opposition candidate Petar Stoyanov, 44, who won 43.93 percent in the October 27 first round, faces Culture Minister Ivan Marazov, the candidate of the governing Bulgarian Socialist Party. Marazov won 26.92 percent in the first round.
The electoral commission says 6.8 million Bulgarians aged 18 and over are registered to vote.

Outgoing President Zhelyu Zhelev lost a U.S.-style primary in June and did not stand for re-election. Parliament elected Zhelev president in August 1990 and he won presidential elections in January 1992. His five-year term of office expires on January 22, 1997 and the new president must be sworn in three days before.

Under its post-communist constitution, Bulgaria is a parliamentary republic in which the president is a mainly ceremonial figure with limited powers. He is commander in chief of the armed forces, he can veto legislation once, and he appoints ambassadors and some state officials.
